author: ashhart
body:
Thank you, @BlivionIaG, and thanks to @millaguie and @ThinkOffApp for the gfx1150 and gfx1151 runs. Between them they found and fixed the `softmax_stats` race, got 30 of 30 greedy replies equal under load, and measured 66.9 tok/s for one Qwen3.6-35B-A3B stream on a Strix Halo.

#463's runtime stays the one HIP runtime, so the engine needs to come in on top of it, in slices, as you planned. The order @ThinkOffApp suggested in #491 works for us: the caps table, the kernels, the Qwen3.5 family on the lane core, then RCCL. Each change to shared code (`lane_host.zig`, the prompt cache, `core/quant`, the registry, the server CLI) needs its own PR with an exactness test, since every backend runs through it. Please carry the build notes from the runs too: `-Dhip-device-lib` for Arch's ROCm layout, and Ubuntu's ROCm 7.1 package lacking rocWMMA's header.

This draft stays readable as the reference, so we'll close it and review the slices as they come.

author: ashhart
body: Thank you, @BlivionIaG. Your gfx1100 and gfx1030 runs, 10,304 affine outputs bit-exact, and @ThinkOffApp's gfx1151 rerun show this runtime works. We're keeping one HIP runtime, the one #463 landed, so we'll close this as superseded by it. Two pieces #463 doesn't have yet are welcome as small PRs on top of it, each with its exactness check: the gfx caps table from RDNA2 to RDNA4, and the `-Dgfx=rdna2,rdna3,rdna3.5` builds.

author: ashhart
body: An update on the order discussed here. #463 stays the one HIP runtime. #492 is closed as superseded by it, with its caps table and RDNA2/RDNA3 builds welcome as small PRs on top of #463. #490's Qwen3.5 engine comes in as slices on #463, in the order @ThinkOffApp gave above: the caps table, the kernels, the Qwen3.5 family on the lane core, then RCCL. This issue tracks those slices until they land.
